title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 57
paragraphs: As for Amompharetos, at first he did not believe Pausanias would ever dare to leave him and his men behind, and he insisted they stay there and not abandon their post; but when Pausanias and his troops were well away in front, then he perceived that they had actually left him behind. He made his division take up their arms and led them slowly toward the main body. This main body, having gone about ten furlongs, waited for Amompharetos's division, halting at the river Moloeis and the place called Argiopion, where also stands a temple of Eleusinian Demeter. It stopped there for this reason: so that, if Amompharetos and his division should not leave the place where they had been posted but should remain there, it might be able to come back to their aid. So Amompharetos and his men were coming up to join them, and the barbarians' cavalry was at the same time beginning to attack them in full force. For the horsemen acted on this day as they had been in the habit of doing every day: seeing the place empty where the Greeks had been posted in the previous days, they rode their horses further and further forward, and as soon as they came up with them began to attack.
